title: spec(i18n): translateObject does not translate validations[].message, so a client reading /meta shows a validation rule's authored message while the server's refusal of the same write is translated
body:
Filing gate **① a defect with a named location**: under a translated locale, a client surface shows the authored validation message while the server's refusal of the same write is translated. Found by the os-dev report on #27099 (comment 6463370569, `out_of_scope_findings`, class **a**). ui seat 2 verified it at `origin/main` `e6e41998` and files it here because the fix sits in `packages/spec/src/**`.

`reach:` named consumer: PR #27133 (`Fixes #27099`). A kanban lane that a blocking `state_machine` rule closes now shows that rule's `message` as its tooltip and its screen-reader description, read from the object served by `/meta`. Any other client surface that reads `validations[].message` from `/meta` has the same gap.

## What is wrong (read at `origin/main` `e6e41998`)

- `packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts` ≈L4044, `translateObject`, overlays `fields` and `actions` from the translation bundle. It never touches `validations`.
- The bundle does address rule messages: `objects.<object>._validations.<rule>.message` (`objectValidationMessageKey`). `os i18n extract` emits that key (`packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-extract.ts` ≈L817–858).
- The only reader of that key is the ObjectQL rule validator (`packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts` ≈L246/L505), so the server's refusal is translated. Nothing under `ui/` reads `_validations`, and `/meta` serves the rule's authored `message`.

## Expected

`translateObject` overlays `validations[].message` from `objects.<object>._validations.<rule>.message` when that key is present, the same way it overlays field labels. A rule with no entry keeps its authored message. A client then shows the same sentence the server's refusal carries, in the viewer's locale.

## Business reason

A zh or ja deployment that translated its validation messages sees them translated in the server's refusal toast. The same rule's explanation on the board (and on any other surface reading `/meta`) stays in the authoring language. The user reads two different sentences, in two languages, for one rule.

## Reader who acts

The `domain:spec` seat, in one PR to `i18n-resolver.ts` with a test, after triage. Who serves `/meta` through `translateObject` decides whether a server-side test is also owed.

## Dedupe

I listed open `domain:spec`, `domain:server` and `domain:i18n` issues and checked titles for translat / locale / i18n. The only hits are #27086 (`apps.APP.label` required) and #27087 (`os lint` bundle fold), both unrelated. **New.**
